sections.markdown:
## C2 — Health and impairment confusables with knowledge-graph hints

FACT_ID: sec05-R01 | anchor: A73
Being 21 or older makes recreational cannabis legal to use, but it never makes driving after cannabis legal, because that ban applies at every age and to any amount. [A73]
Why it matters: group_hint cannabis; prereq_hint sec05-F13; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec05-F18, sec05-F19.
Source: [A73 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec05-R02 | anchor: A74
Whether a drug is prescribed, bought over the counter or illegal changes nothing about impaired driving, which stays a criminal act in every case. [A74]
Why it matters: group_hint medications; prereq_hint sec05-F13; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec05-F20, sec05-F21.
Source: [A74 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec05-R03 | anchor: A74
A heavy machinery warning on a medicine label covers driving a car too, not only factory or construction equipment. [A74]
Why it matters: group_hint medications; prereq_hint sec05-F21; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec05-F22.
Source: [A74 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec05-R04 | anchor: A75
Polydrug use is about combining substances, and the combination can hit harder than any single one, which makes it the leading impairment in fatal crashes. [A75]
Why it matters: group_hint polydrug; prereq_hint sec05-F23; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec05-F24.
Source: [A75 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec05-R05 | anchor: A70
Most drivers may use a hands-free device in one ear, but a driver with an instruction permit or intermediate license may not use any mobile device at all while driving. [A70]
Why it matters: group_hint devices-and-hearing; prereq_hint sec05-F11; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec05-F11, sec05-F12.
Source: [A70 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec05-R06 | anchor: A70
To handle oncoming glare you look to the right edge of the road, while to see farther you keep headlights aimed and slow down so you can stop inside their beam. [A70]
Why it matters: group_hint night-vision; prereq_hint sec05-F07; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec05-F08, sec05-F09.
Source: [A70 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec05-R07 | anchor: A76
The 20-minute nap is the fix when you are already drowsy and alone, whereas stopping about every 100 miles or 2 hours is the plan you make before a long trip. [A76]
Why it matters: group_hint fatigue; prereq_hint sec05-F25; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec05-F27, sec05-F28.
Source: [A76 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec05-R08 | anchor: A75
Hitting rumble strips, drifting from the lane and tailgating are physical driving clues of fatigue, just like heavy eyelids, and each one means pull over and rest. [A75]
Why it matters: group_hint fatigue; prereq_hint sec05-F25; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec05-F26.
Source: [A75 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec05-R09 | anchor: A77
Aggressive driving is defined by intent, a driver purposely endangering people or property or forcing others to protect themselves, and it is classed as a traffic offense. [A77]
Why it matters: group_hint aggression; prereq_hint sec05-F29; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec05-F31.
Source: [A77 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec05-R10 | anchor: A78
Road rage is classed as a criminal offense because the anger turns into violent behavior with a vehicle or another weapon, and it can involve a passenger as well as a driver. [A78]
Why it matters: group_hint aggression; prereq_hint sec05-R09; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec05-F33, sec05-F31.
Source: [A78 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec05-R11 | anchor: A69
Wearing required corrective lenses is a must on every drive, but dark or tinted corrective lenses are the ones to avoid at night. [A69]
Why it matters: group_hint vision; prereq_hint sec05-F05; difficulty_hint 1; confusable_with sec05-F06.
Source: [A69 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0069]
